Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Quizzy runs quizzes during conference talks. A moderator shows the questions on the big screen, and the audience answers on their phones. The first release covers the moderator's side: preparing quizzes.

The design is in `docs/mockups/`, exported from our design tool: a style guide and two screens of this release (the quiz page and the question form), each as a static HTML page (open it in a browser) and a PNG. The stylesheet and the font next to them are the design's assets: use them as they are or adapt them. Follow the look: colors, typography, pill buttons, and layout. Big-screen pages run on LED walls and projectors; player pages run on phones.

The moderator area lives under `/moderate`. Every page in it requires HTTP Basic authentication with the credentials from `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`. Missing or wrong credentials get `401`.

Quizzes:

- `/moderate` lists the quizzes and has the "New quiz" button.
- The quiz form has one field, "Title" (required), and the "Save quiz" button. Saving opens the quiz page.
- The quiz page shows the title and the questions in order. It has the "Add question" button, the "Settings" link and the "Preview" link.
- "Settings" opens the same quiz form for the quiz, and the "Delete quiz" button, which asks for confirmation.

Questions are single-choice with text options. The question form has:

- "Question": the question text (required)
- option rows: each row has a text field labelled "Option 1", "Option 2", and so on, and a checkbox labelled "Option 1 is correct", "Option 2 is correct", and so on. A new question starts with four empty rows. The "Add option" button adds one more row with the next number.
- "Active": a checkbox, on by default
- the "Save question" button

Rules for options:

- Empty rows are skipped.
- A question needs at least two options. Otherwise the form shows "Add at least two options".
- At least one option must be correct (several correct options are fine). Otherwise the form shows "Mark at least one option as correct".
- When a rule fails, nothing is saved and the form keeps what the moderator typed.

Each question on the quiz page shows its text and its options, with the correct options marked. It also has:

- "Move up" and "Move down" buttons that change the order
- the "Active" checkbox: changing it saves at once, with no extra button
- the "Edit" link to the question form
- the "Delete" button, which asks for confirmation

Inactive questions stay on the quiz page, but the preview skips them.

The preview lets the moderator try the quiz as a player would. It goes through the active questions in order, one at a time:

- It shows the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options as buttons.
- Picking an option shows "Correct!" or "Wrong!" and reveals the correct options.
- The "Next question" button opens the next question. After the last question, the "See score" button shows the result, for example "Score: 2/3".
- The "Start over" button restarts the preview. Preview answers are not stored anywhere.

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  OptionRow = Data.define(:body, :correct)

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:position, :id) }
  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }

  normalizes :body, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :position, presence: true, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than: 0 }

  before_validation :assign_default_position, on: :create

  def save_with_option_rows(submitted_rows)
    normalized_rows = Array(submitted_rows).map do |row|
      OptionRow.new(
        body: row[:body].to_s,
        correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct]) || false
      )
    end

    filled_rows = normalized_rows.reject { |row| row.body.strip.empty? }

    valid_self = valid?

    if filled_rows.size < 2
      errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options")
    elsif filled_rows.none?(&:correct)
      errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct")
    end

    return false unless valid_self && errors.empty?

    transaction do
      save!
      options.destroy_all
      filled_rows.each_with_index do |row, index|
        options.create!(
          body: row.body.strip,
          correct: row.correct,
          position: index + 1
        )
      end
    end

    true
  end

  def move_up!
    move(:up)
  end

  def move_down!
    move(:down)
  end

  def move(direction)
    quiz.transaction do
      ordered = quiz.questions.ordered.to_a
      idx = ordered.index(self)
      return unless idx

      target_idx = direction == :up ? idx - 1 : idx + 1
      return if target_idx.negative? || target_idx >= ordered.size

      ordered[idx], ordered[target_idx] = ordered[target_idx], ordered[idx]
      ordered.each_with_index do |question, i|
        new_pos = i + 1
        question.update_column(:position, new_pos) if question.position != new_pos
      end
    end
  end

  private

  def assign_default_position
    return if position.present?

    self.position = (quiz&.questions&.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end
end
EOF

**CSS Cascade Order - A Critical Catch!**

Okay, so I was just looking at the asset pipeline and noticed something slick – Propshaft automatically rewrote that font URL, nice! And I saw that minor `image_processing` warning. It's just complaining about needing libvips, which makes sense since that gem is in the `Gemfile`, even if we aren't using ActiveStorage variants yet. We could remove it or just leave it, it's a minor thing. But the key thing is: *order matters*.

Then I looked at the `stylesheet_link_tag :app` order, and bam! It hit me. `application.css` comes *before* `quizzy.css` alphabetically. On its own, it would seem correct, but it made me think...

Wait a second, there's a CSS cascade issue here! The override `content: none` in `application.css` that targets the correct answer checkmark is getting *overwritten* by the `content: "✓ ";` rule in `quizzy.css` because they have the same specificity, but `quizzy.css` is being loaded later in the cascade. That means `quizzy.css` is overriding `application.css`.

Yes, confirmed! That alphabetical order is biting us.

Now, we have a choice:

1.  We can explicitly load the stylesheets in the *correct* order `<%= stylesheet_link_tag "quizzy", "application", "data-turbo-track": "reload" %>` in both layouts, guaranteeing that `quizzy.css` always loads first, and the override in `application.css` comes last. This guarantees our overrides are always applied.
2. We could just modify the `quizzy.css` file and add our additions at the bottom (also ensuring correct order) or explicitly load the files.

Explicitly loading the stylesheets in that order provides deterministic CSS cascade order.

So, let's fix this in both the `application.html.erb` and `moderate.html.erb` layouts. I'll change both to use that explicit `stylesheet_link_tag` call with the correct order. I'll double-check that `image_processing` warning while I'm at it.

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  OptionRow = Data.define(:body, :correct)

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:position, :id) }
  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }

  normalizes :body, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :position, presence: true, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than: 0 }

  before_validation :assign_default_position, on: :create

  def save_with_option_rows(submitted_rows)
    normalized_rows = Array(submitted_rows).map do |row|
      if row.is_a?(OptionRow)
        row
      else
        OptionRow.new(
          body: (row[:body] || row["body"]).to_s,
          correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct] || row["correct"]) || false
        )
      end
    end

    filled_rows = normalized_rows.reject { |row| row.body.strip.empty? }

    valid_self = valid?

    if filled_rows.size < 2
      errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options")
    elsif filled_rows.none?(&:correct)
      errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct")
    end

    return false unless valid_self && errors.empty?

    transaction do
      save!
      options.destroy_all
      filled_rows.each_with_index do |row, index|
        options.create!(
          body: row.body.strip,
          correct: row.correct,
          position: index + 1
        )
      end
    end

    true
  end

  def move_up!
    move(:up)
  end

  def move_down!
    move(:down)
  end

  def move(direction)
    quiz.transaction do
      ordered = quiz.questions.ordered.to_a
      idx = ordered.index(self)
      return unless idx

      target_idx = direction == :up ? idx - 1 : idx + 1
      return if target_idx.negative? || target_idx >= ordered.size

      ordered[idx], ordered[target_idx] = ordered[target_idx], ordered[idx]
      ordered.each_with_index do |question, i|
        new_pos = i + 1
        question.update_column(:position, new_pos) if question.position != new_pos
      end
    end
  end

  private

  def assign_default_position
    return if position.present?

    self.position = (quiz&.questions&.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end
end

Now, let's get this squared away. I'll make the configuration change and re-run the production `bin/serve` verification script with `.scroll_into_view.click` added to the Ferrum test. require "fileutils"

    browser_options: { "no-sandbox" => nil, "disable-gpu" => nil, "disable-dev-shm-usage" => nil }

    external_requests = []

      status = exchange.response&.status.to_i
      if !url.start_with?("http://127.0.0.1:#{PORT}") && !url.start_with?("data:")
        external_requests << url

      if status >= 400 && !(status == 401 && url.include?("/moderate"))

    page.network.wait_for_idle

        const fonts = Array.from(document.fonts).map(f => ({ family: f.family, status: f.status }));

    page.at_css("input#question_option_rows_1_body").focus.type("Perl CGI")
    page.at_css("input#question_option_rows_0_correct").scroll_into_view.click

    page.network.wait_for_idle

    abort "FAIL: question not saved" unless page.body.include?("What powers Quizzy?")
    puts "PASS: Question saved in production"

    # Verify check mark is not doubled on quiz page
    correct_pill_text = page.evaluate(<<~JS)
      (() => {
        const li = document.querySelector(".question-item__options li.is-correct");
        return {
          text: li.innerText,
          beforeContent: getComputedStyle(li, "::before").content,
          bg: getComputedStyle(li).backgroundColor
        };
      })()
    JS
    puts "Correct pill check: #{correct_pill_text.inspect}"
    abort "FAIL: ::before should be none" unless correct_pill_text["beforeContent"] == "none"
    abort "FAIL: green bg missing" unless correct_pill_text["bg"] == "rgb(0, 179, 107)"
    puts "PASS: Correct option pill styling verified (single checkmark, green bg)!"

    page.network.wait_for_idle
    sleep 0.2
    abort "FAIL: Active toggle did not update count" unless page.body.include?("0 of 1 question active")
    page.reload
    page.network.wait_for_idle
    abort "FAIL: Active toggle did not persist" unless page.body.include?("0 of 1 question active")
    page.at_css("ol.question-list input[type=checkbox]").scroll_into_view.click
    page.network.wait_for_idle
    sleep 0.2
    abort "FAIL: Active toggle on failed" unless page.body.include?("1 of 1 question active")
    puts "PASS: Active auto-save toggle verified in production!"

    # Check Preview at phone viewport (390x844)
    page.resize(width: 390, height: 844)
    page.at_xpath("//a[normalize-space()=\"Preview\"]").scroll_into_view.click
    page.network.wait_for_idle
    sleep 0.2
    abort "FAIL: Preview progress missing" unless page.body.include?("Question 1 of 1")
    mobile_overflow = page.evaluate("document.documentElement.scrollWidth > window.innerWidth")
    abort "FAIL: Mobile preview horizontal overflow!" if mobile_overflow

    page.at_xpath("//button[contains(., \"Ruby on Rails\")]").click
    abort "FAIL: Correct! missing" unless page.body.include?("Correct!")
    page.at_xpath("//button[normalize-space()=\"See score\"]").click
    abort "FAIL: Score: 1/1 missing" unless page.body.include?("Score: 1/1")
    puts "PASS: Mobile preview verified in production (no overflow)!"

    # Also test URL-embedded Basic Auth credentials (http://user:pass@host/moderate)
    page2 = browser.create_page
    page2.go_to("http://#{USER}:#{PASS}@127.0.0.1:#{PORT}/moderate")
    page2.network.wait_for_idle
    abort "FAIL: URL-embedded Basic Auth failed" unless page2.body.include?("Production Talk 2026")

    abort "FAIL: Failed HTTP requests: #{failed_requests}" unless failed_requests.empty?

  ensure

  end

  Process.wait(pid) rescue nil
  FileUtils.rm_f(Dir["storage/production.sqlite3*"])
end

cat <<'EOF' > /app/docs/architecture.md
# Quizzy Architecture Notes

## Overview

Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application backed by SQLite (`storage/<env>.sqlite3`), Hotwire (Turbo + Stimulus via Importmap), and Propshaft for local assets. All design assets (`app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` and `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2`) are served locally without external network dependencies.

## Runtime & Deployment

- `bin/serve` prepares `storage/`, runs `db:prepare` and `assets:precompile`, and executes Puma in the foreground bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT` (`RAILS_ENV=production` by default).
- Production runs over plain HTTP (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`) and accepts any `Host` header (`config.hosts.clear`).
- `GET /up` serves the unauthenticated Rails health check (`200 OK`).
- All persistent data lives under `storage/`.

## Authentication

- All moderator routes live under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`.
- `Moderate::BaseController` enforces HTTP Basic authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using constant-time SHA-256 digest comparison (`ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`). Empty/missing env vars reject with `401`.

## Data Model (Release 1)

- `Quiz` (`quizzes`: `title`) `has_many :questions, dependent: :destroy`
- `Question` (`questions`: `quiz_id`, `body`, `position`, `active`) `has_many :options, dependent: :destroy`
- `Option` (`options`: `question_id`, `body`, `correct`, `position`)

### Notes for Future Releases (Live Runs & Audience Play)

- Currently, editing a question replaces its `options` atomically inside a transaction (`Question#save_with_option_rows`). Once future releases add live game runs and participant answers referencing `option_id` (or snapshotting questions/options per run), either snapshot questions/options when a run starts or update existing options in place by ID to preserve foreign keys.
- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` already contains styling tokens and components for big-screen presentation (`.screen`, `.stage-options`, `.leaderboard`, `.lobby`, `.qr`), participant mobile play (`.play`, `.play-options`, `.play-status`, `.result-card`), and moderator run history (`.runs-table`, `.response-options`).
- ActionCable is currently configured with the `async` adapter in `config/cable.yml` (sufficient for single-process Puma). If multi-worker Puma is ever enabled, switch to `solid_cable` storing its SQLite database under `storage/`.
- Preview (`Moderate::PreviewsController#show` + `preview_controller.js`) runs entirely in client memory from the active questions JSON payload and stores no answers in the database, cookies, or web storage.
EOF
